entities.name: Siege of Tyre
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Siege of Tyre was a pivotal event in the conquest of Alexander the Great. 

 It was a 7-month blockade of the island city of Tyre by Alexander's forces, which ultimately led to the capture of the city in 332 BCE. 

 This event marked the beginning of the Hellenistic period in the ancient Near East, as it allowed Alexander to gain control over the strategic island of Tyre and the surrounding region. 

 As one of the most important cities in the ancient world, Tyre played a significant role in the exchange of goods and ideas between East and West, and its capture paved the way for the spread of Greek culture, language, and philosophy throughout the region. 

 In the words of historian Arrian, 'Alexander, having gained control of the city, ordered a thanksgiving to be held, and distributed 2,000 talents among his soldiers.'
